cells.tense: You are here with the pen, setting down what the unseen work has already taught you.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Take one piece of what you keep private and move one small step of it where it can be seen — one step, no speech, no accounting of what it cost.
cells.core:
You are carrying several things at once, and the work has settled into you: you correct as you go, adjust to what each thing needs, and enough light shows the next step even when the whole road doesn't. That's care that doesn't exhaust and a hold that doesn't clutch. You know when a day's work counted.

Most of this has run underneath other people's plans, and it has been faithful. The gap worth closing is that the ones it's for may not know what was carried unless a piece of it happens where they can see it. Let one piece be visible this week — not a speech, not a tally of hours, just done in the open, then left alone.
cells.sheetLine: Bring one piece of the quiet work into the open.
cells.verb: tending what is growing under your hands through form until it can carry itself
cells.place: a place where the road is only visible one stone ahead and you keep walking

cells.tense: You are already standing in a finished outcome, bracing against the one you can't write in yet.
cells.act: be full for an hour with what was already felt
cells.ask: Sit with the next piece for an hour before you change anything about it — full of it as it stands, not of what it could become.
cells.core:
You are tending something and holding its finished version in your head. That version is vivid, brighter than whatever is actually at hand, and it keeps winning. So the work in progress gets corrected toward the imagined shape, and no current state of it can be rested in because none is the last one. The picture has moved out past the point you're standing at, and what's actually growing under your hands gets measured against a thing that isn't made yet.

Let what you've already made be enough for a while — not because you're done, but because that's how a thing gets to grow. Sit with the next piece for an hour before improving it. Then improve it, or don't. Satisfaction has to land before the next imagining can be made from it.

cells.tense: The work you did sits behind you, and you are still standing where you left off.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: For one more week, make small moves on the thing you set down even when no signal comes — no confirmation, and no waiting for one before you move again.
cells.core:
You are good at this: holding a thing steady, adjusting as it goes, keeping it going through rough stretches. And it has stopped. What used to be steady work now feels like waiting, and the waiting has gone on long enough that the half of you that chose it has gone quiet. You're not absent — your hands know where they were. But the shine is gone and nothing new has started.

Start small and keep it small. A week of small moves on what you set down, made without waiting for a sign, without trying to feel certain first. The direction doesn't return because you feel sure; it returns because the work starts again. You've kept faith this far on hope that's been tested. One more week is a small thing to ask of that.
cells.sheetLine: The work stopped, and hope can start it again.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing in, and the writing goes on without you.
cells.act: let what you gave up be seen by the people it was for, without a word about it
cells.ask: Do your next bit of work where the people it's for can watch it happen, and let what it took show without a word of explanation.
cells.core:
The work is running and other people are being carried by it. They feel it — the thing that keeps going gets kept going. But you've named none of it, and if someone praised you the shrug would be real, because it doesn't register as yours. The apparent source is that's just how it works; the real one is hands that keep at it. What that misnaming costs is quiet: the work drains, because it has no owner.

Don't announce it. Do your next bit where the people it's for can see it happen, and let what it took be seen — no explanation, no bill, no apology for visible effort. They don't need your account of it; they need to have seen it. Then stay for whatever comes after.
cells.sheetLine: The work has hands, and the hands are yours.

attempts.check: The read leans hardest on the mechanism — that the honoring is what's off — but the record never says whether the person has actually named any goal or dream to anyone, so 'you can't say what you're building toward yet' may be wrong for someone who denies wanting anything, and the ask survives that objection because stating a finished thing to no one still works even if the direction is unclear. The unsupported claim is that the infatuation is with the feel of the imaginings rather than the results; the reader could say it's just daydreaming. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person would be any clean aphorism about names coming after the fact.
